raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Part **1/n** of the Kimi K3 / Dist-MoE training stack. Based on `main`: the review diff contains only this feature.

human notes:
previously: `distributed/utils.py::init_distributed()` passes `CommConfig.init_timeout_seconds` to `torch.distributed.init_process_group()` so the world group has, say, 30 minutes timeout. now, that remains unchanged. Additionally, `TrainingEngine._initialize_distributed_runtime()` calls `set_pg_timeouts()` after `ParallelismContext.from_config()`,  so the tracked mesh subgroups get the configured timeout before model/FSDP/optimizer initialization. this also covers the RL trainer. without this pr, independently created NCCL subgroups can still use the default 10-minute timeout even though we configured 30 minutes. the existing switch to `train_timeout_seconds` after the first step is unchanged.

## Why

The world process group receives `comm.init_timeout_seconds`, but mesh subgroups created later do not inherit it. They can retain the backend-default startup timeout through model initialization and the first update.

Example: with `CommConfig(init_timeout_seconds=1800)`, the world group uses 1,800 seconds but a later NCCL subgroup can use its 600-second default. This change applies the configured startup budget to the groups tracked by `ParallelismContext` before model/FSDP/optimizer initialization.

## What changed

- Call the existing `set_pg_timeouts()` helper immediately after `ParallelismContext.from_config()` in the shared training engine.
- Apply the same call in the TorchFT runtime override.
- Preserve the unconditional post-first-step switch to `train_timeout_seconds`, including fake backends.
- Add no helper, configuration field, or test. The deleted forwarding-only mock test is not coverage for the current code.

## User-facing changes

| Configuration | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `init_timeout_seconds=1800` | World: 1,800 s; tracked NCCL mesh groups may use 600 s during startup. | World and tracked mesh groups: 1,800 s during startup. |
| Default `init_timeout_seconds=300` | World: 300 s; tracked NCCL mesh groups may use 600 s. | World and tracked mesh groups: 300 s during startup. |
| After the first update | Existing switch to `train_timeout_seconds`. | Unchanged. |

Groups created separately outside the context's tracked mesh map, including optimizer-specific communicators, are not covered by this call.

## Numerics

No model math, parameter layout, gradient policy, or checkpoint mapping changes. The existing helper adds one startup barrier/device synchronization; there is no new per-update synchronization.

## Testing

Rebased onto upstream `ad7a9937b5e57ccadebbb98b3eb14ff139ceb2b3`. The feature diff is unchanged: ten added lines in the shared engine and TorchFT override.

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --tb=short \
  tests/unit_tests/cpu/test_trainer.py \
  tests/unit_tests/cpu/distributed/test_distributed_utils.py
```

Result: **76 passed**. These existing CPU tests do not directly verify real NCCL subgroup timeout values.

## Known issues / landing gates

All non-type pre-commit checks passed in the preceding review. The three Pyrefly failures were independently reproduced on unchanged upstream: missing `torch_checkpointing.checkpoint_writer.CallbackArgs`, its callback signature mismatch, and optional `video.stream.time_base` multiplication. No unrelated source or dependency workaround is included.


## Stack

Bottom of stack; based on `main`. Next: [#5675](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5675).

**Claude finished @shuhuayu's task in 3m 11s** —— [View job](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/actions/runs/40974907493)

---
**Request changes** -- [review](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5674#pullrequestreview) (move the timeout call into `TrainingEngine` right after the meshes are built, so it covers init and the RL trainer; drop the guard, the helper and the test).

**Claude finished @shuhuayu's task in 1m 7s** —— [View job](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/actions/runs/40978615994)

---
**Approve** (please update the stale PR description before merging): all three earlier must-fix items are resolved -- [review](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5674#pullrequestreview)

**Verdict: Request changes** -- The problem is real, but the fix sits in `Trainer` after `engine.initialize()`. It should go in `TrainingEngine` right after the meshes are built: that covers init itself and the RL trainer, and it is about 5 lines instead of 51.

**What this PR does.** `init_process_group()` gets `comm.init_timeout_seconds`, but the DeviceMesh subgroups created afterwards use the backend default. With no `device_id` bound, they go through `new_group(timeout=None)`, which is 10 min for NCCL. This PR calls `set_pg_timeouts(init_timeout_seconds)` once, after `engine.initialize()`, so the first step runs under the configured budget. The existing switch to `train_timeout_seconds` after step 1 is unchanged.

**Example.**
```
CommConfig(init_timeout_seconds=1800), FSDP 8 + PP 2, NCCL
                    world   subgroups (init)  subgroups (step 1)
main                1800 s  600 s             600 s
this PR             1800 s  600 s             1800 s
engine placement    1800 s  1800 s            1800 s
RL trainer, this PR 1800 s  600 s             600 s
```

### Must fix
1. `torchtitan/trainer.py:240` -- The call is in the wrong layer and runs too late. The meshes are built in `training_engine.py:309`, so model init, FSDP/PP setup, and checkpoint load inside `engine.initialize()` still use the default timeout. `rl/trainer/trainer.py:103` builds `TrainingEngine` directly and gets no fix. Move the call to `_initialize_distributed_runtime`, right after `ParallelismContext.from_config`.
2. `torchtitan/trainer.py:140` -- The `backend != "default"` guard doesn't match the unconditional step-1 call at `trainer.py:522-528`. Drop it and inline the call, or apply it to both calls.
3. `tests/unit_tests/cpu/test_trainer.py:35` -- The mock test only checks the helper's own `if` and argument forwarding. Delete it.

### Should consider
- The default `init_timeout_seconds` is 300 s, which is below NCCL's 600 s default. So for default configs this PR shortens the subgroup timeout during init and the first step from 10 min to 5 min. That matches the field's docstring, but it is a user-visible change for every run, and the description only shows the 1800 s case. Please state it in the before/after table.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- Coverage: `set_pg_timeouts` only reaches one group per axis name in `get_all_one_dimensional_meshes()`. Groups built outside that map are untouched, both by this PR and by the existing train-timeout switch: `build_alternative_fsdp_mesh` split groups, and the per-axis groups of the second and third `_unflatten` calls if DeviceMesh does not dedupe them (the `build_mesh` docstring says it recreates them). This was a gap before this PR; it is worth naming in the description rather than claiming that all DeviceMesh groups are covered.
- The root cause is upstream: DeviceMesh subgroups don't inherit the parent PG's timeout, and `init_device_mesh` / `_unflatten` take no timeout argument. Passing NCCL `Options._timeout` through `backend_override` would be vendor-specific, so setting the timeout after creation is the right local fix. A short comment saying why it is needed is enough.

</details>

Not verified: that `new_group`/`split_group` with `timeout=None` fall back to the backend default in the pinned PyTorch (I could not run Python here), and that `set_pg_timeouts` is safe at engine init under the `fake` backend in CPU unit tests that construct `TrainingEngine`.

A maintainer still needs to review: the PR touches core code.

The fix only takes effect from the first step onward.

    timeout=timedelta(seconds=config.comm.init_timeout_seconds),

```

That is about +5 lines total. It covers init and the first step for both `Trainer` and the RL trainer, and the existing step-1 switch to `train_timeout_seconds` stays as it is.

this PR          1800 s  1800 s            1800 s              train_timeout
RL trainer       same as "this PR"
```

### Must fix

"What changed" says fake and mixed fake-SPMD backends are skipped and a regression test was added. "Testing" describes that test. None of this is in the diff anymore. The default `init_timeout_seconds` is 300 s, so for default configs the subgroup timeout during init and step 1 goes from 600 s (NCCL default) down to 300 s.

### Should consider

TorchFT runs therefore don't get this fix, but they still get the step-1 switch. - The new call adds one startup `barrier` + `synchronize` before `set_determinism`. It runs once per process and adds nothing per step.
- Under `fake` / `real_pp_fake_spmd`, the existing step-1 call already runs `set_pg_timeouts` without any guard, and fake-pg CI exercises that path. So running it unconditionally at init should be safe there too. The CPU unit tests that construct `TrainingEngine` patch `_initialize_distributed_runtime`, so they don't reach this call.
- The gap noted earlier is still there, unchanged by this PR: `set_pg_timeouts` only reaches one group per axis name in `get_all_one_dimensional_meshes()`. Groups created outside that map, such as the `build_alternative_fsdp_mesh` split groups, keep the backend default.

</details>

+            timeout=timedelta(seconds=comm_config.init_timeout_seconds),
+            parallelism_context=parallelism_context,
+        )

reviews.body:
**Verdict: Request changes** -- The problem is real, but the fix sits in `Trainer` after `engine.initialize()`. It should go in `TrainingEngine` right after the meshes are built: that covers init itself and the RL trainer, and it is about 5 lines instead of 51.

**What this PR does.** `init_process_group()` gets `comm.init_timeout_seconds`, but the DeviceMesh subgroups created afterwards use the backend default. With no `device_id` bound, they go through `new_group(timeout=None)`, which is 10 min for NCCL. This PR calls `set_pg_timeouts(init_timeout_seconds)` once, after `engine.initialize()`, so the first step runs under the configured budget. The existing switch to `train_timeout_seconds` after step 1 is unchanged.

**Example.**
```
CommConfig(init_timeout_seconds=1800), FSDP 8 + PP 2, NCCL
                    world   subgroups (init)  subgroups (step 1)
main                1800 s  600 s             600 s
this PR             1800 s  600 s             1800 s
engine placement    1800 s  1800 s            1800 s
RL trainer, this PR 1800 s  600 s             600 s
```

### Must fix
1. `torchtitan/trainer.py:240` -- The call is in the wrong layer and runs too late. The meshes are built in `training_engine.py:309`, so model init, FSDP/PP setup, and checkpoint load inside `engine.initialize()` still use the default timeout. `rl/trainer/trainer.py:103` builds `TrainingEngine` directly and gets no fix. Move the call to `_initialize_distributed_runtime`, right after `ParallelismContext.from_config`.
2. `torchtitan/trainer.py:140` -- The `backend != "default"` guard doesn't match the unconditional step-1 call at `trainer.py:522-528`. Drop it and inline the call, or apply it to both calls.
3. `tests/unit_tests/cpu/test_trainer.py:35` -- The mock test only checks the helper's own `if` and argument forwarding. Delete it.

### Should consider
- The default `init_timeout_seconds` is 300 s, which is below NCCL's 600 s default. So for default configs this PR shortens the subgroup timeout during init and the first step from 10 min to 5 min. That matches the field's docstring, but it is a user-visible change for every run, and the description only shows the 1800 s case. Please state it in the before/after table.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- Coverage: `set_pg_timeouts` only reaches one group per axis name in `get_all_one_dimensional_meshes()`. Groups built outside that map are untouched, both by this PR and by the existing train-timeout switch: `build_alternative_fsdp_mesh` split groups, and the per-axis groups of the second and third `_unflatten` calls if DeviceMesh does not dedupe them (the `build_mesh` docstring says it recreates them). This was a gap before this PR; it is worth naming in the description rather than claiming that all DeviceMesh groups are covered.
- The root cause is upstream: DeviceMesh subgroups don't inherit the parent PG's timeout, and `init_device_mesh` / `_unflatten` take no timeout argument. Passing NCCL `Options._timeout` through `backend_override` would be vendor-specific, so setting the timeout after creation is the right local fix. A short comment saying why it is needed is enough.

</details>

Not verified: that `new_group`/`split_group` with `timeout=None` fall back to the backend default in the pinned PyTorch (I could not run Python here), and that `set_pg_timeouts` is safe at engine init under the `fake` backend in CPU unit tests that construct `TrainingEngine`.

A maintainer still needs to review: the PR touches core code.

**Verdict: Approve -- please address the items below before merging.** The code now matches the suggested fix: one `set_pg_timeouts(init_timeout_seconds)` call in `TrainingEngine._initialize_distributed_runtime`, right after the meshes are built (+6 lines). What's left is the PR description, which still describes the old version.

**Earlier must-fix items**
1. Wrong layer / runs too late (`trainer.py:240`): **resolved**. The call is now at `training_engine.py:313`, so it covers model init, FSDP/PP setup and checkpoint load. It also covers `rl/trainer/trainer.py`, which builds `TrainingEngine` directly.
2. `backend != "default"` guard only on one call: **resolved**. The guard and the helper are gone, and the new call is unconditional, the same as the step-1 call at `trainer.py:501`.
3. Mock-only test: **resolved**. It was deleted.

**Example.**
```
CommConfig(init_timeout_seconds=1800), FSDP 8 + PP 2, NCCL
                 world   subgroups (init)  subgroups (step 1)  after step 1
main             1800 s  600 s             600 s               train_timeout
this PR          1800 s  1800 s            1800 s              train_timeout
RL trainer       same as "this PR"
```

### Must fix
1. The PR description is stale and no longer matches the code. The human notes say "`Trainer.__init__()` calls `_apply_initial_process_group_timeouts()` after `engine.initialize()`". "What changed" says fake and mixed fake-SPMD backends are skipped and a regression test was added. "Testing" describes that test. None of this is in the diff anymore. Please update it to: one call in `_initialize_distributed_runtime`, applied on every backend, no new test. While you are editing it, also put the default-config change in the before/after table. The default `init_timeout_seconds` is 300 s, so for default configs the subgroup timeout during init and step 1 goes from 600 s (NCCL default) down to 300 s.

### Should consider
- `torchtitan/experiments/torchft/trainer.py:68` overrides `_initialize_distributed_runtime` without calling `super()`. TorchFT runs therefore don't get this fix, but they still get the step-1 switch. If you want them to match, add the same 4-line call after `ParallelismContext.from_config` at `torchft/trainer.py:105`. That edit stays inside the experiment, so it doesn't touch core.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- The new call adds one startup `barrier` + `synchronize` before `set_determinism`. It runs once per process and adds nothing per step.
- Under `fake` / `real_pp_fake_spmd`, the existing step-1 call already runs `set_pg_timeouts` without any guard, and fake-pg CI exercises that path. So running it unconditionally at init should be safe there too. The CPU unit tests that construct `TrainingEngine` patch `_initialize_distributed_runtime`, so they don't reach this call.
- The gap noted earlier is still there, unchanged by this PR: `set_pg_timeouts` only reaches one group per axis name in `get_all_one_dimensional_meshes()`. Groups created outside that map, such as the `build_alternative_fsdp_mesh` split groups, keep the backend default.

</details>

Not verified: a GPU run confirming subgroup timeouts after init (needs NCCL).

A maintainer still needs to review: the PR touches core code.
